column3: The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name three times and the breach-of-faith root in noun and verb; BSB uses “Him” for the middle divine name and says “committed this breach of faith.”
The Hebrew says they returned from the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead and then brought a report; BSB makes that origin the subject matter of the report with “regarding.”
The Hebrew names “the sons of Israel” twice and says the report was “good in their eyes”; BSB names “the Israelites” once and says they were satisfied.
The Hebrew has no separate explicit name after the naming verb; BSB supplies the name “Witness” before also translating the explanation that it is a witness.
